findings.title: Signal filter infrastructure is shipped although the PR says it was removed.
findings.body: The PR description says it was narrowed to two changes (drop `MODEL_CHUNK` spans in CloudExporter, default log level `warn`). It says it removed the "signal filter infrastructure" and the processor observability work. This diff still adds a public `signalFilters` option for spans, logs, metrics, scores and feedback, plus errors-only/tripwire processor filtering in the default span filter. That is new public API the stated request does not cover. Remove it, or update the request if it is meant to ship.

findings.title: The `metrics.autoExtract` control was added although the description says it was removed.
findings.body: The PR description lists "metrics auto-extract controls" as removed from this PR. The diff still adds a `metrics.autoExtract` config, with its schema in `config.ts` and type in `core.ts`, and a new branch in `emitSpanEnded` that skips auto-extracted metrics. This new config surface and code path is not part of the two requested default changes.

findings.title: A new public `Processor.observability` option and runner/workflow changes go beyond the stated request.
findings.body: The description says processor-level observability work was removed and deferred to a follow-up design. The diff still adds `observability?: boolean | 'errors-only'` to the public `Processor` interface. It also rewires span creation and TripWire span handling in `runner.ts`, `workflows/workflow.ts` and `workflows/evented/workflow.ts`, and adds `processorObservability`/`processorOutcome` attributes to `ProcessorRunAttributes`. This is new public API in shared core code that the request does not ask for, and it changes tripwire span behaviour for every processor.

findings.title: TripWire aborts no longer mark legacy processor spans as errors.
findings.body: Before this change, every legacy runner path (input, input step, output, output step, output stream, request error) ended a TripWire span with `processorSpan.error({ error, endSpan: true, ... })`. The removed comment said this was "so it shows as ERROR in traces". `endTripWireProcessorSpan` now calls `span.end()` with attributes only, so `errorInfo` is never set. This applies to every processor, not only `errors-only` ones. Any exporter, dashboard or alert that checks span status or `errorInfo` will now count a blocked request (for example a PII guardrail abort) as a success. The cloud filter only works around this by also reading `processorOutcome`. If tripwires should still read as errors, keep `span.error(...)` and add `processorOutcome: 'tripwire'` to its attributes.

findings.title: Dropping successful errors-only processor spans leaves their child spans without a parent.
findings.body: The `observability: 'errors-only'` docs say these spans exist so that "processor-internal work can nest under them". For example, an LLM call or agent run inside the processor gets the processor span as its parent. This filter drops only the `PROCESSOR_RUN` span itself. Its children still go to cloud with a `parentSpanId` that was never uploaded, so the trace tree in cloud has orphaned subtrees and broken parent links. Either drop the whole subtree, which needs the decision at span-creation time, or re-parent children to the dropped span's parent before export.

findings.title: Playground import reordering is still present despite the description saying it was removed.
findings.body: The description says the "playground import churn" was removed. This file and `pages/traces/trace/index.tsx` still have import-reordering-only changes unrelated to the observability defaults. Revert them to keep the PR to its stated scope.
